description: A single action offered by an action surface — the F5 TmMobileActionBar, the F4 overflow toolbar, and any future action host. The model is deliberately free of rendering concerns: a host maps an item to a button, a menu entry, or another surface.

properties.name: Id
properties.description: Stable identity of the action (used as a render key). When empty, Label identifies the item. Must not start with 'tm-' when it lands in a CSS class or id — that prefix is reserved for library-internal stems.

properties.name: Label
properties.description: The user-visible label. Names the rendered button and stays fully in the DOM.

properties.name: Icon
properties.description: Optional icon name (an IconNames value or a registered icon).

properties.name: Priority
properties.description: Overflow rank ONLY — it never changes the render order. The bar and the "More" menu render in the order of Items; the items beyond the visible budget move into the menu by ascending priority (the lowest priority overflows first, ties drop the last item first). Disabled items still count towards the budget.

properties.name: Overflow
properties.description: Pins the item to the surface or to the overflow menu independently of Priority: Never keeps it on the surface (it counts against the visible budget), Always puts it in the "More" menu even when the budget would show it (it does not count), Auto (default) lets the budget and the Priority rank decide.

properties.name: Danger
properties.description: Marks a destructive action. The overflow menu tints the entry with the danger colour so a destructive item keeps its meaning when it leaves the surface.

properties.name: Checked
properties.description: The action's on/off state when it is a toggle. null (default) is a plain action — a menuitem in the "More" menu. true/false make it a menuitemcheckbox with aria-checked and a check mark in the menu, and add aria-pressed to its tile on the mobile action bar. Activating it still runs OnClick (and closes the menu like every entry); the host flips the state in the callback.
properties.example:
new() { Id = "grid", Label = "Grid", Checked = _gridOn,
         OnClick = EventCallback.Factory.Create(this, () => _gridOn = !_gridOn) }

properties.name: CheckedMixed
properties.description: Renders a toggle whose Checked is false as partially on (aria-checked / aria-pressed = "mixed"). Ignored when Checked is null or true.

properties.name: Disabled
properties.description: Disables the action. Disabled items render as disabled buttons/menuitems.

properties.name: Group
properties.description: Stable key of the group the action belongs to in the "More" menu. Consecutive items (in Items order — grouping never reorders) with the same non-empty key render as one role=group section named by GroupLabel, and adjacent runs are divided by a role=separator. Null or empty means ungrouped. No effect on the surface itself.

properties.name: GroupLabel
properties.description: Accessible name and visible header of the item's group in the "More" menu, read from the FIRST item of a run. Empty renders the run without a group wrapper (separators only).

properties.name: OnClick
properties.description: The action itself. Invoked exactly once per user activation. Create the callback with EventCallback.Factory.Create(this, …) — the receiver is the owning component, so its markup re-renders automatically when the action mutates state; a default (empty) callback is a no-op.

properties.name: KeepMenuOpen
properties.description: When true, the "More" menu stays open after the action runs — use for actions that open another surface (a confirm dialog, a picker): the surface promotes AFTER the sheet, so it paints above it (top-layer order = open order), and closing it returns focus to this item. The default closes the sheet BEFORE the action runs: focus returns to the "More" trigger and the action runs with no menu bookkeeping behind it.
